column2: Foreword written by Alfred Upham for book by Swasdi Nitibhon on the topic of dance, undated
column3: In a book regarding dance written by Miami alum Swasdi Nitibhon, one of the cohort of Thai students, president Upham wrote a forward on the shared cultural experience of dance. Thai students at Miami University in the early 20th century seemed to have been well received by the University population; they were not only interested in learning about American culture but had been excellent students academically.

This storied program notably hosted a plethora of Thai students during the 1930s and 40s, proving themselves to be excellent students and overall exceptional Miamians. This program, even having Thai royalty amongst its cohorts, would experience troubles during the Second World War due to Thai relations with the Japanese government.

column2: Letter from Alfred Upham to Murray Sheehan regarding invitation to a minister from Thailand to deliver commencement speech, 19 November 1941

column2: Letter from Alfred Upham to K. Tomizawa requesting to meet in San Francisco before departing for vacation abroad, 19 October 1937
column3: Several weeks before President Upham's departure for San Francisco and from there, Japan, Upham addresses a letter to accomplished Miami alum, Kiyoshi Tomizawa. A priority in Upham's travels to Asia was to meet with alumni that lived in Asia, including Tomizawa who Upham hoped to have a conversation with in San Francisco before abruptly leaving on a ship bound for Japan, perhaps not only could they catch up on Tomizawa's career but his personal experience as a Japanese person.

column2: Letter from Alfred Upham to WN Jardine regarding his upcoming travels and travel advice, 20 October 1937
column3: In preparation for his eventual stay in Egypt during his Asian sabbatical, President Upham reaches out in this letter to President William Jardine of the University of Wichita, a well traveled expert and scholar on Egyptian and Middle Eastern subjects. President Upham addresses the problems that he has had to organize this trip to Asia, including the forgoing of China due to the Japanese invasion at the time, as well as his lack of experience in certain countries. President Upham ends the letter by stating that while he wants special treatment where he travels as an academic, he also wishes to avoid unwanted publicity to not be seen as wasting University funding.

column2: Letter from C.V. Hibbard to Alfred Upham regarding the deferment of Nisei students studying STEM subjects, 21 February 1944
column3: In a national effort to increase the amount of students enrolled in STEM programs across the country military development purposes, C.V. Hibbard writes to President Upham and other institutions with Nisei Japanese students present in the student population. With quotas in place to have a certain number of STEM students, institutions are defering Japanese students who had shown promise in the STEM field. Hibbard reminds Upham and others that they are to instead treat Japanese students like any other regarding STEM enrollment.
